messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (to English) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------|--------| | Tant' | “so” (intensifier) | Tiom | “so much / so” | OK | | è | 3sg present of *essere* “to be” | estas | “is / is” | OK | | amara | adjective “bitter” | amara | “bitter” | OK | | che | conjunction introducing result clause | ke | “that” | OK | | poco | adverb “little, slightly” | iom | “a little / slightly” | OK | | è | 3sg present of *essere* | estas | “is” | OK | | più | comparative adverb “more” | pli | “more” | OK | | morte | noun “death” | morto | “death” | OK | | ma | coordinating conjunction “but” | Sed | “but / however” | OK | | per | preposition of purpose “in order to” | por | “for / in order to” | OK | | trattar | infinitive “to treat / to discuss” | trakti | “to treat / to discuss” | OK | | del | contraction *di + il* “of the” | la | “the” (definite article) | OK | | ben | noun “good” | bono | “good” | OK | | ch'i' | relative pronoun + 1st‑person pronoun “that I” | kiun mi | “that I (acc.)” | OK | | vi | adverb “there” (locative) | tie | “there” | OK | | trovai | 1sg past “I found” | trovis | “found” | OK | | dirò | 1sg future “I will say” | Mi diros | “I will say” | OK | | de | preposition “of / about” | pri | “about” | OK | | l'altre | “the other (plural)” | la aliaj | “the other” | OK | | cose | noun “things” | aferoj | “things / matters” | OK | | ch'i' | relative pronoun + 1st‑person pronoun “that I” (plural object) | kiujn | “that (acc. pl.)” | OK | | v' | clitic for *vi* “there” | tie | “there” | OK | | ho | auxiliary *avere* used in perfect | — (omitted) | (no direct equivalent) | **UNNECESSARY** | | scorte | past participle “seen” | vidis | “saw / have seen” | OK |
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: **ho** – the auxiliary verb *avere* has no counterpart in Esperanto; the perfect is expressed simply with the past tense **vidis**, so the auxiliary is omitted.
All other source words are accounted for with appropriate Esperanto equivalents; no missing, wrong, or grammatical‑agreement errors were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Esperanto script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
